rv.q: Then in the middle, and at the play’s centre, 39-year-old Mary needs to be understood. Played by Polly Lister, wise and yet vulnerable, she is the clever high-flyer, the one who became a doctor, receiving admiration, yearning for love.

It is a quietly powerful piece following three sisters who reunite in their childhood home on the evening before their mother’s funeral, focusing on grief, family dynamics, and the subjectivity of memory. With each sister remembering their childhood differently, will this production stick in the mind, or is it one to be forgotten?
